Preserve existing data on request failure or an empty replacement of a nonempty view, and continue accepting the unchanged v1 store layout without copies or migration.

Split end_of_day into pricing/<ticker> and manifests/<ticker>; atomically publish one pending update.json containing inclusive from/to session dates with the verified pricing transaction. New incremental notices cover only actually changed sessions, not the request window or unchanged later rows; extend unconsumed ranges, replace with the entire range on full refresh, and create no notice for unchanged data. Full replacement invalidates old, new, and pending date extents including removed sessions. Add repeated symbol, CSV/line file, tracked-universe, non-truncating from-date, inclusive to-date, and force-download CLI options with per-ticker batch failure isolation; preserve explicit exclusive request-end and refresh-all aliases. Force reacquires after recovery and can replace damaged owned payloads while trusting intact receipts. Make initial store publication atomic and retry transient transport failures without adding durable stores or audit trees.

Run at most three ticker workers, each owning one complete ticker acquisition/publication boundary. Share one thread-safe, smoothly paced 199-request-per-rolling-minute budget across all requests, probes, pages, and retries, with a shared cooldown honoring numeric or HTTP-date Retry-After responses, including exhausted 429 attempts. Add --workers 1/2/3 (default 3), bounded ticker scheduling, completion progress, and input-ordered batch summaries. Keep the v3 datastore layout and existing ticker locks/handoff unchanged, and accept v4 source validators without re-reading cold payloads.

Preserve the v3 layout, ticker lock/notice protocol, and readability of v1-v5 pricing boundaries and validators.

Guard planned replacement under the ticker publication lock against a changed source receipt or date span; retain existing recoverable publication, pending lineage notices and automatic check-summary updates.

Select the latest exchange session strictly before the current America/New_York date for automatic downloads, freezing one end per CLI batch. Use the existing exchange calendar across weekends, holidays and daylight-saving changes; fail closed outside calendar coverage.

Apply the New York midnight completion cutoff to explicit inclusive and exclusive ends as well. Preserve UTC request boundaries, symbol-mapping dates, existing v1-v10 publications and all pricing/lineage handoff formats.

Add a dedicated approved-history append stage that consumes the existing minimal summary handoff and requests only missing completed sessions in all eight views. Batch compatible ranges with the existing solver labels, up to 8000 symbols within URL and memory budgets, with complete pagination and no repeated historical probes or full-month acquisition.

Freeze one symbol selection for registration, durable work and pricing execution so mutable input files cannot introduce unregistered acquisitions.
